reviewer_notes: Differentiated career roles are discussed, so A's not_discussed is wrong and its blank evidence/page are not excused. Article Fourteen (Vacancies and Promotions) A.1 enumerates in-unit promotional positions - Elementary Reading Supervisors, Elementary Teaching Assistant Principals, School Psychologists, Building Level Instructional Coordinator, Reading/Math Supervisors, Elementary Physical Education Coordinator (PDF p. 23, footer 22) - with Section E making a Master's degree a mandatory qualification for Department Heads, Reading Supervisors and others and Section D giving preference to teachers already employed (PDF p. 24); Appendix B attaches index differentials to those same roles plus Mentors (Plus.33) and Title I Supervisor (PDF pp. 42-44); Art. Twelve B.3-B.4 gives Department Heads/Building Level Instructional Coordinators a longer 185-day year (PDF p. 21); Appendix A.A creates a mentor program and Art. Seven C a joint committee on National Board certification. Searches run: career ladder/advancement/step/lane, master teacher/lead teacher/differentiated, department head/stipend, mentor/instructional coach, plus text scans for 'team leader' and 'career ladder' (both absent as phrases). B's quote of Art. Fourteen A.2 is verbatim and correctly placed on PDF p. 23 (printed footer 22, so the footer diverges by one here); it is a subsection of the same Section A that defines promotional positions and establishes that such positions carry salary beyond the Appendix A schedule, so it supports the answer, though A.1's list of named positions would have been the stronger anchor. Note this is a promotion/role-differentiation structure, not a formal multi-stage career ladder with defined advancement stages - the only stage-like progression is the step-and-lane salary schedule (Appendix B) - but the question's 'differentiated career roles' branch is satisfied, so yes is the right status.
